newsitem.title: USA: Eight nations to discuss ground transport security.
newsitem.headline: Eight nations to discuss ground transport security.

text.p: Officials of the world's seven major industrial democracies and Russia will meet next spring to discuss ways to improve ground transportation anti-terrorism measures, the United States said on Tuesday.
The meeting was needed, U.S. Transportation Secretary Federico Pena said, because "More than ever, transportation systems are being singled out as targets of terrorism."
Pena said security officials at the meeting, to be held in Washington, would focus on improving the prevention, investigation and response to terrorism, and on improved cooperation among governments.
He said the decision to hold the meeting was made at the end of a Washington meeting this week of land transportation officials of the eight nations.
The eight, in addition to the United States and Russia, were Canada, Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Japan.

Pena said that major attacks against transportation last year included a series of bombings in subways in Baku, Azerbaijan which killed dozens of people and injured hundreds; the derailment of an Amtrak passenger train in the United States that killed one and injured 78; the bombing of a Paris subway station that killed seven and wounded more than 80; a bus bombing in Israel that killed eight and injured 50, and the gas attack in the Tokyo subway that killed 12 amd injured 5,500.
